article: What does a driving-simulator nap study tell you about alertness right after waking?
Read the short-term takeover outcome and distinguish it from a general safety finding.
Original automated-driving simulator study of post-sleep performance. No personal safety advice.
copy: A post-nap simulator study tests how people perform a defined task after sleep. That is more specific than asking if they feel refreshed. Its measurements apply to the simulator and the intervals the researchers tested.
Check what task started immediately after waking

When you read an alertness claim, check elapsed time after waking and whether participants also did a comparison task without a nap. A strong result on one task does not automatically predict what happens in traffic, especially when fatigue or unfamiliar conditions differ.
This research does not certify a safe waiting time. The evidence is useful for distinguishing a short-lived post-wake state from the rest of the night.

article: Can a sleep wearable measure heart rate accurately and still miss HRV?
Read a validation study using separate heart-rate and heart-rate-variability comparisons.
Original validation of six wearables against reference sleep and heart measurements in healthy adults.
copy: Heart rate describes beats per minute. Heart-rate variability uses variation in the timing between beats. Small errors in beat timing can matter for variability even if average beats per minute look similar. A published validation compared these outputs separately across six wearables.
Two outcomes can disagree in one device

The result depends on whether the device and its comparator used the same time window. Read the model, algorithm version and quality of the signal before borrowing a device result. Also check whether reported agreement describes group averages or individual readings.
Use this distinction when comparing algorithms. The study does not turn a wearable estimate into a clinical assessment.

Were intervals measured accurately enough for the particular variability calculation?

article: Why can a watch track your pulse well but estimate calories poorly?
Compare two measures from a laboratory validation of wrist-worn devices.
Shcherbina et al. original laboratory comparison of commercially available wrist devices and reference measures.
copy: A wrist device can estimate heart rate from its sensor and then use a separate model to estimate energy expenditure. An original lab comparison found that energy-expenditure estimates generally had larger errors than heart-rate estimates. Accuracy on one output did not establish accuracy on the other.
Ask whether the validation tested the same output

The researchers compared multiple activities and devices against reference outcomes. Watch error can change with activity type, model and conditions. Find the actual error measure for the output you are using. A different unit, such as average beats per minute, cannot take the place of a calorie error estimate.
Use device calories as rough estimates when a source does not validate the same model and activity.

article: Can lying down change the heart-rate recovery number after a workout?
Check how body position and activity during recovery change the conditions under which pulse is measured.
Original exercise studies that compared different recovery states and postures.
copy: Heart-rate recovery records how heart rate changes after stopping or reducing exercise. Comparisons can change when one measurement is taken while sitting and another while walking or lying down. Human studies have tested several of those recovery conditions directly.
Match the conditions in repeated measurements

In a diary, preserve the type of exercise, time from the end and what you did during the measurement. Without that information, an apparent change may reflect the protocol. For example, one minute of walking can be different from one minute of resting after the same effort.
This is a measurement comparison. Do not use a single home number to diagnose a change in fitness or health.

article: Why can the second downhill run feel easier to recover from in a study?
Check whether a trial accounted for participants becoming accustomed to the exercise itself.
Original human studies of repeated downhill running and subsequent performance or soreness outcomes.
copy: Muscle responses after a repeated downhill run can differ from responses after the first one. Original repeated-bout studies track the same kind of exercise across sessions to investigate that pattern. Any product comparison using repeated bouts has to consider what participants already did.
Do not confuse session order with a product effect

If everybody does the unfamiliar run first without a product and repeats it with a product later, the treatment and session order change together. Compare randomized ordering and the time between sessions before attributing the difference. The precise outcome matters as well. A change in soreness does not necessarily equal a change in performance.
Keep the training type and participant experience with the conclusion.

article: Is a carbohydrate mouth-rinse trial evidence about drinking a sports drink?
Distinguish tasting and expelling a solution from consuming it during an exercise protocol.
Original human cycling studies of carbohydrate mouth rinsing with distinct exercise conditions. No fueling prescription.
copy: In a rinse study, the exposure is a solution in the mouth that is then expelled. An exercise result under those conditions does not estimate how much carbohydrate or fluid someone ingested. A trial that asks participants to drink the same product would test another intervention.
Check whether the tested solution was swallowed

Chambers and colleagues examined cycling and responses to oral carbohydrate. Another paper used a glycogen-reduced condition and did not report the same performance result. These procedures and participants were not interchangeable. Look for the tested exercise endpoint and the method of administering the solution.
If a headline says a sports drink worked, read the methods before treating the result as evidence about a full serving of that beverage.

article: Is a timed sleep sound experiment the same as playing pink noise all night?
See how a closed-loop study uses an EEG signal to time sounds against sleep activity.
Original closed-loop auditory slow-wave studies. No home sound exposure recommendation.
copy: Closed-loop sleep research delivers sounds in response to a measured brain signal under specified conditions. A video that plays background noise continuously does not use the same timing information. A finding about slow-wave activity under timed stimulation therefore applies to a narrower procedure.
The timing signal is part of the treatment

Some experiments compare pulses timed to the phase of a sleep oscillation with another timing or control condition. To interpret an effect, look for the recording device, sound timing and measured outcome. More of a measured signal in a test interval does not itself establish better sleep or better next-day performance.
Check whether the advertised product actually reproduced any part of the experiment beyond playing a similar sound.

article: Why did a school starting 55 minutes later add less than 55 minutes of sleep?
Read the original Seattle school start-time study and distinguish timetable changes from recorded sleep.
Original Seattle observational before-after study of high school start times and actigraphy.
related: See how to keep a sleep diary
copy: After Seattle delayed the high school start by 55 minutes, the study reported an increase of about 34 minutes in median sleep duration. The schedule change sets the opportunity. Sleep behavior still depends on when students fall asleep, wake up and use the extra time.
A schedule is an opportunity, not a measurement

The researchers used activity-based measurements and compared student groups across school years. The study did not assign start times randomly to individual students. Treat other results, such as changes in school performance, as separate observations with their own possible contributors.
When quoting the study, keep the time change and the sleep estimate in separate units. Both are measured in minutes, but they answer different questions.

article: Why is travel jet lag different from shifting your sleep on weekends?
Distinguish a change in external time zone from changes in a weekly sleep schedule.
CDC travel-health reference and original social jetlag research. No individualized travel or treatment schedule.
related: See how to keep a sleep diary
copy: A traveler who crosses time zones encounters a different local clock. Someone who sleeps later on days off can change their sleep timing while the local clock stays the same. Both shifts may involve a mismatch between sleep and other schedules, but the exposures are different.
Use the correct clock for each comparison

The CDC’s travel guidance describes disruption after rapid travel across time zones. Social jetlag studies instead compare sleep timing on work and free days. For travel, check direction, time zones and local arrival time. For weekly sleep, find the reported sleep measurements and midpoint calculation.
An example schedule can describe timing. It does not measure a person’s internal clock by itself.

article: Do two workouts with the same duration have the same recorded training load?
Read and calculate the session-RPE measure using two hypothetical workouts.
Foster et al. original session rating method. Hypothetical scores illustrate multiplication, without exercise prescription.
copy: In a session-rating approach, training load can be estimated by multiplying duration by the athlete’s rating for the whole session. Two 40-minute workouts with different ratings will therefore give different scores. The result uses an arbitrary unit, rather than calories or measured mechanical work.
Keep duration and perceived effort visible

For a 40-minute session rated 4, the score is 160. Rating 7 gives 280 at the same duration. A session of 70 minutes rated 4 also gives 280, but that equivalence comes from the scoring rule. It does not make the training stimulus identical.
If a recovery study uses the method, record the scale and when participants gave their ratings before comparing scores.

article: What did a sleep mask experiment measure besides time asleep?
Read the next-day memory and attention outcomes instead of treating an eye mask as a quantified sleep extension.
Original overnight eye-mask experiments and next-morning cognitive outcomes.
related: See how to keep a sleep diary
copy: An eye-mask study assessed what people did on learning and alertness tasks after different nights. That is separate from measuring whether total sleep increased. The same paper can record sleep-related measures and next-day behavior without those outcomes becoming equivalent.
Separate the overnight exposure and next-day test

Find out whether the comparison mask blocked light in the same way and which outcome was tested. A memory task performed the next morning is not a direct readout of every overnight sleep stage. The context also matters for extending the result to other bedrooms, products or ages.
Use the study as evidence about its specific mask conditions and the tasks measured.

article: Why can a sleep watch miss time spent awake without moving?
Read an insomnia-device validation by the difference between quiet wake and actual sleep.
Original laboratory validation of consumer and research-grade activity trackers against polysomnography in participants with insomnia.
related: See how to keep a sleep diary
copy: Some activity-based devices may interpret quiet wake as sleep. That matters when a person lies still for long stretches. An original study compared wearable measures with laboratory polysomnography in people with insomnia, a setting where the distinction is especially relevant.
Check wake detection separately from sleep detection

Overall agreement can look satisfactory because the night contains substantial time asleep. If your question concerns wake after sleep onset, look specifically for how accurately the device identifies wake periods. Keep the sample and tested device with the numbers. Both may differ from a product sold later with revised software.
A lower displayed number of awakenings does not by itself show fewer awakenings occurred.
table: Check the validation result you need
How often was reference sleep detected?

Could errors cancel out in the nightly sum?

article: Why does the same bright light have different effects depending on when it is tested?
Read a human phase-response experiment by internal circadian timing instead of one universal alarm time.
Original human bright-light phase-response studies. No personalized light treatment guidance.
copy: A light exposure can shift circadian timing in different directions depending on the part of the internal cycle when it occurs. In phase-response experiments, researchers relate exposure to measured circadian markers. They do not merely assign a universally meaningful wall-clock hour.
Internal phase is not the same as local clock time

Two people who see light at the same clock time can be at different points in their internal rhythms. To interpret an experiment, read how the researchers determined phase, when the light was delivered and what subsequent marker changed. The test’s duration and conditions also matter.
These study results explain differences between experimental schedules. They do not set a treatment time for an individual.
